pairs.difference: A: the oil lamp is shot dead-frontal at eye level and perfectly symmetric. The base ellipse is almost flat and the object has no turn at all, so it reads like a front elevation (planar_share 0.003, below the real range). B: the flashlight sits on a strong diagonal and is turned three-quarters, so the lens face foreshortens into an ellipse. That matches the turned bottle in the real cards.
pairs.fix: Turn the lamp about 30 degrees and tilt it slightly. Raise the camera a little so the top of the base and the rim of the glass chimney show as clear ovals, not flat lines.

pairs.difference: A: the police car is a small, whole object set in a full street scene. Sidewalk, road and buildings are all equally sharp and recede to a far horizon, which is the 'whole object on a staged base' look the generated lesson cards have. B: the bike is cropped tight, with the car rear filling the card. The bike's flat side profile matches the rack plane, so it holds one consistent view.
pairs.fix: Move the camera closer and lower so the car fills the card. Drop the far buildings to a simple soft backdrop and keep only a strip of road under the wheels.

pairs.difference: A: the vending machine is at eye level with a slight turn showing its left side and no top face, and it stands on a soft floor-to-wall sweep. B: the tape roll stands on edge in three-quarter view, with its loose tail lying flat on the same ground plane. Both hold one view with mild perspective. B's planar_share (0.62) is slightly high, but that comes from the flat side of the roll, not from a camera error.

A: the wallet lies flat under a near-overhead camera, and the wood planks run at one shallow angle, so it is consistent. B: the book is seen from high above, showing a huge cover face, while the page block and spine at the bottom-left are seen almost side-on. The bookmark tabs on the right stick out flat toward the viewer. Planar_share 0.706 is above the real range.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera so the book cover is shorter and the spine and page edges show more. Keep the bookmark ribbons lying in the same tilted plane as the book.

pairs.difference: A: the dog is a complete figure centered at ground level, and its grass plane meets a flat striped backdrop at a horizon around mid-height. B: the boxing gloves are a tight, edge-cropped close-up on a wooden table, with the table edge and wall seam consistent. A weak call: A's fitted-whole-object staging leans toward the generated lessons.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera slightly higher and closer so the dog fills more of the card. Make the grass a short foreground strip, not a wide field running to the backdrop.

pairs.difference: B: the floor planks under the binoculars spread out sharply toward the bottom of the card, giving a wide-angle, forced-perspective floor. The barrels face the viewer head-on, while the floor is seen from high above. A: the magnifier and map lie on one top-down plane, and the wood planks run at a single mild angle.
pairs.fix: Use a longer lens: draw the floor planks almost parallel, with only slight convergence. Turn the binoculars so they lie along the planks, seen from above at the same angle as the floor.

pairs.difference: A: the ship's hull shows its open interior and ladder from above, but the portholes and side planks are drawn straight side-on. The masts lean in different directions and the bowsprit points up-right, so the parts do not share one view. B: the spyglass is a single three-quarter cylinder whose rings foreshorten evenly toward the eyepiece.
pairs.fix: Draw the ship from one three-quarter angle, slightly above the waterline. Keep all masts upright and parallel, with the deck and hull side foreshortened together.

pairs.difference: A: the camera floats at a mild three-quarter angle, with the top face (green in the normals) and the right side visible and the lens ellipse matching the body turn. B: the player floats tilted, with its front face and right edge visible, and the earbud cord trails in the same space. Both have mild perspective and one consistent view.

B: the sneakers are a side-by-side pair seen almost head-on, and the floor/wall seam sits high on the card at a hard horizon. Both shoes face the same way, posed like a symmetric product shot. A: the hat sits on a soft sweep at a mild three-quarter angle from slightly above, and its brim ellipse matches its crown.
pairs.fix: Turn the shoes about 30 degrees and stagger them, one ahead of the other. Replace the hard wall line with a soft gradient floor.

pairs.difference: B: the doorknob is a macro close-up. The backplate is drawn as a perfectly flat, front-on rectangle, but the knob sphere is shifted left and shows its rosette, as if seen from the left. A room in deep perspective is visible through the doorway on the right. Planar_share 0.53 is above the real range. A: the door is a frontal, flat elevation framed by ivy.
pairs.fix: Show the knob and backplate from the same slight side angle, with the plate drawn as a narrow, slanted rectangle. Replace the deep room behind with a soft wall color.

pairs.difference: A: the planter table is a full garden scene. The paving runs in perspective, there is a sharp picket fence behind and side bushes, and the near and far legs show a slightly high camera. B: the sunscreen bottle stands frontal at eye level with the glasses in front on one floor line. Weak call, A's staged complete scene leans toward the generated lessons.
pairs.fix: Move the camera closer so the planter fills the card. Simplify the fence and bushes into a soft background and keep just a small patch of paving under the legs.

pairs.difference: A: the bag lies on the wood seen from above, but its outline is a skewed parallelogram. The zip strip at the top runs at a different tilt from the bottom edge, and the ring inside is seen more steeply than the bag around it. Planar_share 0.807 is well above the real range. B: the racket and ball lie on the court seen from a high three-quarter angle, and the court line recedes at the same angle.
pairs.fix: Draw the bag as a clean rectangle lying flat, with its top zip edge parallel to its bottom edge. Draw the ring lying inside it at the same overhead angle.

pattern: On viewpoint and depth, generated cards give themselves away in three ways. They stage the hero as a complete, centered object on a full scene base (street, garden, island). They lean on frontal or symmetric product-shot views. And their parts drift between views, such as a frontal plate with an oblique knob, or a hull drawn from above with portholes drawn side-on. Real cards crop tighter, use one mild three-quarter turn, and keep the backdrop simple.
